name: Mexico: highlands and the south
tagline: Pre-Hispanic cities, baroque towns, markets, and cool cloud-forest hiking in community-run villages.

access.route: Brussels→Mexico City via Paris, Amsterdam or Madrid (Aeroméxico, KLM, Air France), 11–12 h

nightsNote: 8–12°C in the Sierra Norte cabins, 12–15°C in Mexico City and San Cristóbal, 20°C in Oaxaca
whyNotes: The richest history of the seven and a Latin America trip Mom will recognise and love. Rainy season means clear mornings, a storm at 4 pm, and green mountains; it also keeps most tourists away from the highlands.
fitNotes: Altitude stays under 3,300 m (Mexico City is 2,240 m, Oaxaca 1,550 m). Heat only appears if you go down to Palenque. The Guelaguetza in Oaxaca (19 and 26 July 2027) is a festival to build around, but it fills the town: book early or avoid those two weekends.

blocks.name: Mexico City
blocks.place: Anthropology museum, Templo Mayor, Coyoacán, Teotihuacán
blocks.history: Aztec capital under a colonial one
see: Museo Nacional de Antropología (half a day minimum)
Templo Mayor and the cathedral on the Zócalo
Coyoacán: Frida Kahlo house (book), Trotsky house
Teotihuacán at opening time (8 am) to beat the heat and the buses
Chapultepec castle, Palacio de Bellas Artes murals
blocks.note: Altitude 2,240 m: take the first day slowly. Afternoon storms, so museums after 3 pm.

blocks.name: Puebla + Cholula
blocks.place: Talavera baroque city, the largest pyramid by volume
see: Capilla del Rosario
Amparo museum
Cholula pyramid tunnels and the church on top
Mole poblano where it was invented

blocks.name: Oaxaca
blocks.place: Monte Albán, Mitla, markets, mezcal, Guelaguetza
see: Monte Albán early morning
Santo Domingo church and the cultural museum (Tomb 7 treasure)
Mitla mosaics and a Teotitlán weaving workshop
Mercado 20 de Noviembre, Benito Juárez market
Mezcal palenques in Santiago Matatlán
blocks.note: Guelaguetza Mondays 19 and 26 July 2027: superb, and the town is full for both weekends. Bus from Mexico City 6 h or a 1 h flight.

blocks.name: Hierve el Agua + Tule
see: Hierve el Agua mineral pools (go at opening)
El Tule cypress
Teotitlán del Valle rugs

blocks.name: Guanajuato
blocks.place: Silver-mining city of tunnels and alleys
see: Alhóndiga museum (1810 uprising)
Callejoneadas at night
Valenciana mine and church
Diego Rivera's birthplace museum

blocks.name: San Cristóbal de las Casas
see: San Juan Chamula church and Zinacantán weavers (with a local guide)
Na Bolom museum
Sumidero canyon boat (half day)
Amber museum, textile centre
blocks.note: Fly Mexico City or Oaxaca to Tuxtla (1.5 h), then 1 h up the hill.

blocks.name: Palenque + Agua Azul
blocks.place: Maya city in rainforest, turquoise cascades
see: Palenque ruins at 8 am, Temple of the Inscriptions
Agua Azul and Misol-Ha on the way
blocks.note: Hot and humid; the one stop over Mom's heat line. Five hours of mountain road from San Cristóbal.

blocks.name: Sierra Norte: Pueblos Mancomunados
see: Cuajimoloyas to Latuvi or Benito Juárez on footpaths between villages
Cloud forest, agave fields, miradores over the valley
Cabins and meals run by the comunidad; local guide mandatory and excellent
Horse or bike options for the easier days
blocks.note: Cool, green, no crowds, 1.5 h from Oaxaca. One of the best things in southern Mexico and almost nobody does it.

blocks.name: Lagunas de Montebello + El Chiflón
blocks.place: Pine-forest lakes near the Guatemalan border, waterfall trail
see: El Chiflón waterfall staircase walk
Lagunas de Montebello colour lakes by raft
Chinkultic ruins above the lakes

blocks.name: Valle de Bravo
blocks.place: Lake town and pine forests west of Mexico City
see: Monte Alto forest walks
Velo de Novia waterfall
Lakeside evening

blocks.name: Copper Canyon by the Chepe train
blocks.place: Chihuahua to Los Mochis; canyons four times the size of the Grand Canyon
see: Chepe Express between Creel and El Fuerte
Divisadero rim walks and the cable car
Day walks with Rarámuri guides near Creel
Urique or Batopilas at the canyon bottom (hot, optional)
blocks.note: Spectacular, but far: flight to Chihuahua, 9 h of train. Rainy season is the greenest time. Adds about €280 in flights.

blocks.name: Huasteca Potosina
blocks.place: Turquoise rivers and waterfalls, Edward James's surrealist garden
see: Tamul waterfall by canoe
Las Pozas garden at Xilitla
Puente de Dios
blocks.note: Hot and humid; here for completeness, not for Mom.

notes: Rainy season in the highlands: clear mornings, a storm around 4 pm, 20–28°C days. Plan outdoor hours before lunch.
Hurricane season on both coasts; this routing stays inland on purpose.
Mexico City and Oaxaca museums are busiest at weekends; weekdays are calm.

lodgingAssumption: Local B&B or Airbnb, two rooms for five, one meal out a day; shared van or hire car
